source.title: Benchmarking and Understanding Compositional Relational Reasoning of LLMs
source.authors: Ruikang Ni; Da Xiao; Qingye Meng; Xiang-Yu Li; Shi-Hui Zheng; Hong-Liang Liang

record.file_problem: The full paper is present. Some PDF-extracted text and figures are flattened, but this does not prevent reading the relevant text and tables.
record.tranche_reason: The paper identifies and analyzes generalized induction-head circuits in Vicuna-33B, and explicitly distinguishes them from the traditional induction-head pattern. This refines the mechanism claim, but does not test training-time formation or the original canonical copying behavior.
record.gate_note: The paper uses attribution patching to identify induction-head classes in GAR circuits and reports their head identities and functional descriptions. Results cited from Olsson et al. and other work are not included as study results. Intervention results that jointly modify induction heads with other head classes are not treated as isolated evidence about induction heads.
record.test_reason: The paper builds a compositional reasoning benchmark (GAR) and traces Vicuna-33B circuits with attribution patching. It labels some heads 'induction heads', but redefines them: they attend to the token syntactically following a semantically related earlier token, not the canonical [A][B]…[A]→[B] copy. It never tests canonical induction behaviour, previous-token composition, training dynamics, the token-index loss share, or cross-model presence. The induction-head rows are lists of heads selected by the authors' attribution, not results on whether any version holds. The generalized-induction finding is recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record overweights induction heads. The authors' main conclusions concern other findings. First, GAR is challenging for LLMs and the compositionality gap grows with scale. Second, Vicuna-33B reuses core circuits across GAR tasks. Third, True/False heads encode truthfulness across models and datasets. As a secondary point, they say generalized higher-order induction heads bridge head classes across context in the ICL sub-circuit.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes pretrained Vicuna-33B on synthetic GAR tasks using attribution patching; it does not reproduce the original induction-head training experiment or its training-dynamics measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: The studied tasks vary in relation schema and affirmative/negative form; the identified head sets vary across tasks, as listed separately in Tables 6 and 7.

fits_no_version.finding: In Vicuna-33B GAR circuits, 'induction heads' attend from a query to the token syntactically following an earlier semantically related token. 'Higher-order induction heads' (e.g. 16.10, 15.4) carry signals from the one-shot demonstration and bridge relating heads to predicting and local heads. Their matched attention weights stay high across easy and hard tasks (Fig. 4a).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In large pretrained LLMs, generalized (semantic-relation) induction heads and higher-order induction heads that carry demonstration signals form a reusable in-context learning sub-circuit across related few-shot tasks.

record.problems: The induction-circuit evidence is concentrated on Vicuna-33B and eight selected GAR tasks chosen because the model could solve them with high accuracy. The attribution analysis is manually guided, and the paper says it does not use automatic circuit-discovery methods. The canonical induction-copying task and training dynamics are not evaluated.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant induction-head rows were omitted. Joint intervention results in Figure 4 are excluded because interventions combine induction heads with other head classes, so the reported task-performance changes do not isolate induction-head effects.

untested.parts: Canonical [A][B]…[A]→[B] copying; composition with a previous-token head; small attention-only transformers.
All: no measure of the share of in-context learning (loss vs token index) carried by induction heads.
All: the cross-size Vicuna experiments concern True/False heads, not induction heads.
All: no variation of data or training.
All: no comparison of induction heads with other mechanisms for few-shot task learning.

missing.what: Average matched attention weights of Ind. and Ind.2 heads on same,same vs other,other tasks. Ind.2 heads are described as robust, with a negative gap. Relevant only to the fits_no_version construct.

record.verdict_notes: The record's V1 labels (limits_scope on R1–R9) are dropped. The rows are head selections under a redefined construct, not tests of V1. Excluding the joint Ind.+Loc.2 interventions is correct: they do not isolate induction heads. The study is peer-reviewed at AAAI 2025.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test the canonical [A][B] … [A] → [B] copying task or the proposed composition with an earlier previous-token head in small attention-only transformers; its induction heads are studied in GAR on Vicuna-33B.
No training-time formation, abruptness, loss bump, or token-index loss comparison is measured.
The paper does not measure whether induction heads account for most in-context learning, or loss falling with token index, in large transformers.
The paper studies induction circuits in Vicuna-33B; its cross-size intervention experiments concern True/False heads, not induction heads.
No comparison of data or training setups for induction-head formation or persistence is reported.
The paper does not compare induction heads with other mechanisms as carriers of few-shot task learning.
No training transitions or sub-steps in induction-head formation are measured.

conditions.value: GAR circuits; zero-shot and few-shot distinctions discussed

rows.baseline: Traditional induction heads are described as attending to the immediate next token after a previous occurrence of the current token.
rows.value: GAR induction heads attend to the next syntactically related token after a previous token that is semantically related to the current token; higher-order induction heads carry in-context signals across the few-shot demonstration.
rows.locator: Appendix E, “Explanations on Types of Heads in Circuits”; Section “Circuits in Generation Tasks”
rows.note: This is an explicit generalization of the traditional induction-head pattern, not a direct test of canonical [A][B] copying.
rows.check: This is the authors' definition of their generalized induction-head class, a different construct from V1. It is not a test of the [A][B] mechanism or of previous-token composition. Belongs under fits_no_version.
